sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Dilemma
sections.description: This section introduces the specific case of a young male presenting with hyperglycemia, establishing the core diagnostic challenge of distinguishing Monogenic Diabetes (MODY) from Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes. It details the patient's demographic profile, physical exam findings, family history patterns characteristic of autosomal dominant inheritance, and initial laboratory abnormalities including the paradox of glycosuria without ketosis.
subtopics: Patient demographics and referral context (young adult with incidental hyperglycemia)
Physical examination findings: Normal BMI vs. absence of acanthosis nigricans
Analysis of three-generation family history: Early-onset pattern across generations
Initial lab profile: Elevated HbA1c (10.2%), fasting/post-prandial glucose, and presence of glycosuria
Absence of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) despite severe hyperglycemia

sections.section_title: Pathophysiological Mechanisms and Differential Diagnosis Strategy
sections.description: This section bridges the gap between clinical presentation and diagnosis by exploring the underlying biology of HNF1A-MODY. It contrasts the pathophysiology of beta-cell dysfunction against insulin resistance (Type 2) and autoimmune destruction (Type 1), outlines the utility of functional testing like C-peptide stimulation, and establishes the algorithmic approach to ruling out common diabetes types before proceeding to genetic testing.
subtopics: Genetics of MODY: Role of HNF1A as a transcription factor in pancreatic beta-cells and renal tubules
Mechanism of glycosuria in HNF1A-MODY: Reduced renal threshold via SGLT2 downregulation
Differentiation from Type 1 Diabetes: Significance of negative autoantibodies (GADA, IA-2A)
Differentiation from Type 2 Diabetes: Interpreting C-peptide levels and lack of insulin resistance markers
Interpretation of Glucagon Stimulation Test results regarding residual beta-cell function

sections.section_title: Confirmatory Genetic Testing and Variant Interpretation
sections.description: Focusing on the pivotal step of molecular diagnosis, this section details the use of Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) panels to confirm HNF1A-MODY. It specifically addresses the identification of a novel heterozygous mutation (p.N270S), discussing how pathogenicity is established when variants are absent from standard databases like ClinVar, utilizing ACMG guidelines and segregation analysis.
